dhcp_ownership_evidence_health: The gap T0106 exposed is closed. Because address ownership is decided from Kea's leases, DHCP is a SAFETY AUTHORITY on this appliance and its silence is a safety condition - and the old surface asked only whether Kea answered status-get, which a server with no lease manager does perfectly, for days. netd now probes the authority by READING THE LEASES on every health request, and classifies three conditions separately because they need three different responses: LEASE_MANAGER_UNAVAILABLE (the exact .25 condition, matched on Kea's own 'no current lease manager is available'), LEASE_QUERY_FAILED (any other refusal or outage), and MEMFILE_STATE_UNUSABLE (the on-disk cause, which outranks the symptom and names the artifact - the zero-byte <leasefile>.pid that memfile refuses to open its database without). An evidence outage DEGRADES the reported enforcement plane and sets kea_healthy=false, so neither health nor a deployment check can call the guest plane healthy while its ownership authority is unavailable. deploy/scripts/check-dhcp-ownership-evidence.sh is the operational equivalent, and check-phase3-enforcement-plane.sh refuses a session-minting surface whose evidence cannot be read. NOTHING REPAIRS ANYTHING: no file is deleted, truncated or renamed and no service is restarted, because a check that silently repairs the authority it judges destroys the evidence and hides a recurring fault. Coverage: seven Go regression tests reproducing the live replies and the zero-byte artifact (including that the probe leaves both files untouched), a six-case operational self-test driven against a fake Kea control socket, a new enforcement-plane self-test case, and nine offline preflight assertions - including one that fails if the probe ever gains a mutation call. Preflight is now 83/83.
